purpose: machine-readable ontology of running operations and managing execution as evaluable work units across process management (lean, six-sigma, theory-of-constraints, throughput, quality control), supply chain (forecasting, inventory, procurement, logistics, resilience), organizational management (structure, delegation, hiring, performance), and goals/metrics (OKRs, KPIs, balanced scorecard, dashboards, operating cadence), as a subdomain node of business strategy and operations for a knowledge-searcher meta-KB.
assumptions: Operations & Management is modeled as a subdomain of Business Strategy & Operations.
Nodes are concrete, evaluable operational/management work units (methods, decision areas, control mechanisms), not topics.
No observed dataset or experimental evidence is supplied; all numeric values are heuristic priors.
Scope follows standard operations-management framing (Slack/Brandon-Jones & Johnston, Operations Management) plus lean, six-sigma, theory-of-constraints, S&OP, OKR, and balanced-scorecard practice.
exclusions: Corporate and competitive strategy formulation itself (covered by the parent business-strategy subdomain).
Detailed financial accounting, capital budgeting, and corporate finance.
Marketing, sales, and product strategy beyond their demand and goal inputs to operations.
Deep statistical method theory and data-engineering infrastructure beyond their use in operations.

competency_questions.question: How does business strategy translate into an operating model, competitive priorities, and goals?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OPS_STRATEGY_ALIGNMENT and GOAL_SETTING_OKR define operating model and cascaded goals

competency_questions.question: What is the end-to-end value stream and where is value added vs wasted?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROCESS_MAPPING produces a value stream with waste classification

competency_questions.question: Which step is the system constraint that governs throughput?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BOTTLENECK_ANALYSIS identifies the constraint from the map

competency_questions.question: How should improvement effort be focused to raise throughput?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BOTTLENECK_ANALYSIS and LEAN_IMPROVEMENT target the constraint

competency_questions.question: How is defect rate and process variation reduced and improvement controlled?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: QUALITY_CONTROL and CONTINUOUS_IMPROVEMENT_GOV control variation and changes

competency_questions.question: How are the right metrics defined, surfaced, and kept honest?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: KPI_METRIC_SYSTEM and DASHBOARD_REPORTING define and render metrics with guardrails

competency_questions.question: How is future demand forecast and matched to capacity?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEMAND_FORECASTING and CAPACITY_PLANNING reconcile demand and capacity

competency_questions.question: How is inventory policy set to hit a service level at minimum cost?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INVENTORY_MANAGEMENT sets policy from forecast and error

competency_questions.question: How are suppliers selected and supply risk and continuity managed?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROCUREMENT_SOURCING and OPS_RISK_RESILIENCE manage supplier and disruption risk

competency_questions.question: How are goods moved and stored to meet service at minimum landed cost?
How does the operating cadence turn metrics into decisions and follow-through?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OPERATING_CADENCE produces decisions and tracked actions from KPIs and dashboards

competency_questions.question: How is the organization structured and capacity staffed to execute the model?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ORG_STRUCTURE_DESIGN, CAPACITY_PLANNING and HIRING_STAFFING align structure and people

competency_questions.question: How are decisions delegated and performance managed without losing control?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DELEGATION_DECISION_RIGHTS and PERFORMANCE_MANAGEMENT assign authority and manage output

competency_questions.question: How do goals, KPIs, and the scorecard stay aligned to strategy and balanced across perspectives?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GOAL_SETTING_OKR, KPI_METRIC_SYSTEM and BALANCED_SCORECARD keep measurement aligned and balanced

glossary.definition: the configuration of people, process, and assets that delivers the strategy
the full set of steps that take a product or service from request to delivery
the single step whose capacity limits total system throughput
how reliably a stable process meets specification (Cp/Cpk)
the cross-functional plan reconciling demand, supply, inventory, and capacity
inventory held to absorb demand and lead-time variability at a target service level
full cost of a purchase including quality, risk, and logistics, not just unit price
who is empowered to make, be consulted on, or escalate each decision class
an outcome objective with measurable, time-bound key results
a metric that predicts a future lagging outcome
the disciplined rhythm of reviews that drives decisions and follow-through

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from standard operations-management and management literature (Slack, Brandon-Jones & Johnston, Operations Management; Goldratt, The Goal; Womack & Jones, Lean Thinking; Kaplan & Norton, Balanced Scorecard; Doerr, Measure What Matters) and common practice; no measured dataset supplied.
does_not_support: measured forecast error or service levels
grounding_limits: all numeric values are heuristic priors, not measurements
no observed or experimentally_validated labels are eligible

normalization_definitions.rounding: round computed scores to 2 decimals; tolerance 0.02

nodes.definition: Translate business strategy into an operating model, competitive priorities, and capacity posture before any process or metric is designed.
contradictors: efficiency-only manager who optimizes locally without strategy

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when business strategy or competitive priorities shift

pros.claim: anchors every process, supply-chain, and metric choice to strategy
pros.example: choosing a responsiveness priority forbids a pure lowest-cost sourcing decision

cons.claim: a wrong or vague operating model makes downstream optimization optimize the wrong thing
cons.example: running lean cost programs while strategy demands flexibility starves capacity

failure_modes: competitive priorities left implicit
operating model copied from a non-comparable firm
acceptance_tests: operating model and competitive priorities written before process design
capacity posture stated and approved

nodes.definition: Document the end-to-end value stream, process steps, hand-offs, and value-add vs waste so improvement targets are grounded in the real flow.
contradictors: manager who improves steps without mapping the whole flow

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the process is redesigned or a new product line is added

pros.claim: exposes the real flow so improvement is aimed at the binding constraint, not a felt symptom
pros.example: a VSM reveals a 3-day queue before inspection that no one had quantified

cons.claim: a stale or idealized map sends improvement at the wrong step
cons.example: mapping the documented process instead of the actual one hides the real bottleneck

failure_modes: map reflects intended not actual process
handoffs and rework loops omitted
acceptance_tests: map validated against observed runs
value-add vs waste classified for each step

nodes.definition: Identify the system constraint that governs throughput using Theory of Constraints so capacity and improvement effort target the binding limit.
contradictors: manager who improves non-constraints and expects throughput gains

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when demand or the process changes the location of the constraint

pros.claim: focuses scarce improvement effort on the only step that moves system throughput
pros.example: adding capacity at the constraint lifts output where non-constraint gains do nothing

cons.claim: misidentifying the constraint wastes investment and can shift the bottleneck unseen
cons.example: buying a faster machine upstream just grows the queue at the real constraint

failure_modes: non-constraint optimized for local efficiency
constraint moves after a change and is not re-found
acceptance_tests: constraint confirmed by utilization and queue data
non-constraints subordinated to the constraint

nodes.definition: Apply lean methods (kaizen, 5S, flow, pull) to remove non-value-add waste and stabilize flow at and around the constraint.
contradictors: batch-and-queue manager optimizing machine utilization

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when flow stabilizes and a new waste source dominates

pros.claim: removes queues and waste, cutting lead time without new capital
pros.example: a pull system cuts WIP and exposes the next problem to solve

cons.claim: local lean gains away from the constraint do not improve throughput and can starve it
cons.example: a 5S blitz on a non-constraint cell looks productive but moves no output

failure_modes: improvement applied off the constraint
standard work not sustained after the event
acceptance_tests: lead-time or WIP reduction measured
standard work in place and followed

nodes.definition: Reduce defect rates and process variation using SPC and six-sigma (DMAIC) so output meets specification capably and predictably.
contradictors: ship-and-inspect manager who tolerates rework

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when defect rate or process capability drifts out of control

pros.claim: makes output predictable and reduces costly rework and escapes
pros.example: a stable Cpk above 1.33 lets the process run without 100% inspection

cons.claim: chasing variation everywhere wastes effort where defects do not hurt the customer
cons.example: tightening a non-critical dimension adds cost without improving the product

failure_modes: acting on common-cause noise as if special-cause
capability claimed from an out-of-control process
acceptance_tests: process shown statistically in control before capability is reported
CTQs tied to customer/spec requirements

nodes.definition: Estimate future demand and translate it into a sales-and-operations plan that balances supply, inventory, and capacity.
contradictors: plan-by-last-year manager ignoring signal and error

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when forecast error exceeds tolerance or demand regime shifts

pros.claim: drives inventory, capacity, and procurement off one reconciled plan
pros.example: an S&OP plan stops sales and operations working to different volume numbers

cons.claim: overconfident point forecasts hide error and cause stockouts or excess
cons.example: planning to a single number with no error band guarantees periodic shortfalls

failure_modes: forecast error not measured
S&OP not reconciled across functions
acceptance_tests: forecast reported with error bounds
S&OP plan reconciled across sales, ops, finance
revisit_triggers: new product or channel changes demand

nodes.definition: Set inventory policy (reorder points, safety stock, lot sizes) to meet a target service level at minimum holding and shortage cost.
contradictors: just-fill-the-shelf buyer ignoring carrying cost

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when service level misses or carrying cost exceeds plan

pros.claim: hits a chosen service level at the lowest total inventory cost
pros.example: sizing safety stock to demand variability and lead time beats a flat days-of-cover rule

cons.claim: policy set on a bad forecast amplifies stockouts or dead stock
cons.example: safety stock built on an under-stated forecast error still stocks out

failure_modes: safety stock decoupled from forecast error and lead time
one policy applied across A/B/C items
acceptance_tests: service level and total cost computed for the policy
policy differentiated by item class

nodes.definition: Select, contract, and manage suppliers to secure the right cost, quality, and risk profile for purchased goods and services.
contradictors: lowest-unit-price buyer ignoring total cost and risk

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when supplier risk, cost, or quality crosses a threshold

pros.claim: secures total cost, quality, and continuity rather than just unit price
pros.example: dual-sourcing a critical part avoids a line-down event when one supplier fails

cons.claim: single-sourcing on price creates an irreversible dependency and supply risk
cons.example: a sole supplier with no alternative can halt production at renewal

failure_modes: selection on unit price not total cost of ownership
critical part single-sourced with no contingency
acceptance_tests: supplier evaluated on total cost, quality, and risk
critical items have a contingency or second source
revisit_triggers: spend or criticality of a category changes

nodes.definition: Move and store goods through warehousing, transportation, and network design to meet service at minimum landed cost.
contradictors: cheapest-freight buyer ignoring service and reliability

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when service misses or landed cost exceeds plan

pros.claim: balances delivery speed/reliability against freight and facility cost
pros.example: a regional DC cuts last-mile time at a known fixed-cost tradeoff

cons.claim: optimizing freight alone degrades service and inflates expedites and returns
cons.example: slow cheap freight on time-critical orders triggers costly expedited recovery

failure_modes: mode chosen on freight cost ignoring service
network not revisited as demand geography shifts
acceptance_tests: service level and landed cost evaluated together
network reviewed against current demand geography

nodes.definition: Size and schedule capacity (people, equipment, hours) to meet demand at a chosen utilization and service buffer without chronic overload.
contradictors: run-at-100-percent-utilization manager ignoring variability

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when utilization or lead time leaves the planned band

pros.claim: matches capacity to demand variability so lead time stays stable
pros.example: holding utilization below 90% on a variable line keeps queues from exploding

cons.claim: planning to full utilization makes lead time blow up under any variability
cons.example: loading a variable process to 98% turns small surges into long queues

failure_modes: capacity planned to average demand ignoring variability
utilization pushed so high lead time becomes unstable
acceptance_tests: plan accounts for demand and process variability
utilization target leaves a queue/lead-time buffer

nodes.definition: Design reporting lines, spans of control, and decision rights so the organization can execute the operating model with clear accountability.
contradictors: reorg-by-personality manager ignoring decision rights

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the operating model or scale makes the structure misfit

pros.claim: aligns accountability and decision rights with how work actually flows
pros.example: clear decision rights stop two managers each assuming the other owns a call

cons.claim: frequent reorgs are highly disruptive and reset coordination and trust
cons.example: a structure change every two quarters destroys institutional knowledge

failure_modes: structure misaligned with decision flow
reorg done without a decision-rights map
acceptance_tests: decision rights mapped before structure is locked
span of control checked against coordination load

nodes.definition: Assign who decides, who is consulted, and what is escalated so execution moves fast without losing control of high-stakes choices.
contradictors: everything-needs-my-approval bottleneck manager

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when escalations or stalled decisions reveal misplaced authority

pros.claim: speeds routine decisions while keeping high-stakes ones reviewed
pros.example: a clear approval threshold lets a team commit spend below it without delay

cons.claim: over-delegating irreversible/high-risk calls causes costly uncontrolled mistakes
cons.example: delegating a one-way-door decision with no review leads to an unrecoverable error

failure_modes: high-risk decisions delegated without review
trivial decisions escalated, creating a bottleneck
acceptance_tests: irreversible/high-risk classes carry a review gate
escalation thresholds defined by decision class
revisit_triggers: a delegated decision causes a major miss

nodes.definition: Define roles and run a structured selection process that fills capability gaps with reliable, low-bias hiring decisions.
contradictors: gut-feel interviewer using unstructured chats

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when role fit or hiring quality data shows the process is mis-selecting

pros.claim: structured selection predicts performance far better than unstructured interviews
pros.example: a job-relevant work-sample plus scorecard reduces a costly mis-hire rate

cons.claim: a bad hire is slow and expensive to reverse and damages a team
cons.example: a mis-hire in a key role costs months of disruption and re-recruiting

failure_modes: unstructured, biased selection
role defined vaguely so the wrong profile is sought
acceptance_tests: role scorecard defined before sourcing
selection uses structured, job-relevant evaluation

nodes.definition: Set expectations, give feedback, and review performance so individual and team output stays aligned with goals and standards.
contradictors: annual-review-only manager who never gives interim feedback

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when expectations or goals change, or feedback stops changing behavior

pros.claim: keeps individual output aligned to goals through frequent, specific feedback
pros.example: weekly coaching on a clear expectation corrects drift before a review cycle

cons.claim: metric-only reviews drive gaming and demoralize when context is ignored
cons.example: rating people purely on a single number invites optimizing the number not the goal

failure_modes: feedback only at annual review
performance judged on gameable single metrics
acceptance_tests: expectations tied to goals and stated in advance
feedback given continuously, not only at review

nodes.definition: Set a small number of outcome goals and key results that cascade strategy into measurable, time-bound objectives for teams.
contradictors: task-list manager who tracks activity not outcomes

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when strategy shifts or goals stop driving real prioritization

pros.claim: cascades strategy into a few measurable outcomes teams can prioritize against
pros.example: three clear key results let a team say no to work that does not move them

cons.claim: too many goals, or output goals miscast as outcomes, dilute focus and invite gaming
cons.example: fifteen 'priorities' tied to compensation become a checklist no one truly drives

failure_modes: too many objectives to focus
activity metrics set as key results
acceptance_tests: objectives are few and outcome-based
key results are measurable and time-bound
revisit_triggers: a goal becomes a gamed target

nodes.definition: Define a coherent set of leading and lagging KPIs with clear definitions and targets that measure operational and strategic health.
contradictors: vanity-metric manager tracking what looks good

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a metric is gamed or stops predicting the outcome it proxies

pros.claim: balances leading and lagging signals so problems are caught before lagging results move
pros.example: a leading quality metric warns weeks before the lagging escape rate climbs

cons.claim: a single optimized metric gets gamed and distorts behavior (Goodhart)
cons.example: rewarding call-handle-time alone shortens calls and tanks resolution quality

failure_modes: vanity metrics with no decision attached
single metric optimized without a guardrail
acceptance_tests: each KPI has an owner, definition, and target
gameable KPIs paired with a counter-metric

nodes.definition: Organize metrics across financial, customer, process, and learning perspectives so management balances short-term results with long-term capability.
contradictors: finance-only manager tracking only the P&L

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when one perspective dominates and others are starved

pros.claim: prevents over-optimizing finance at the expense of customer, process, and capability
pros.example: a process-and-learning view funds capability that pure P&L tracking would cut

cons.claim: a scorecard with no causal logic becomes a disconnected metric grab-bag
cons.example: four lists of metrics with no strategy map give balance in name only

failure_modes: perspectives not causally linked
one perspective dominates in practice
acceptance_tests: each perspective has linked, causal metrics
no single perspective starves the others

nodes.definition: Build trustworthy dashboards and reports that surface the right metrics to the right decision-makers with correct, timely data.
contradictors: everything-on-one-screen reporter who buries the signal

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a dashboard shows wrong/stale data or no decision uses it

pros.claim: puts the few decision-relevant metrics in front of the right people on time
pros.example: a focused exec dashboard drives a weekly decision instead of a 40-tile data dump

cons.claim: a wrong or stale dashboard is worse than none because it is trusted
cons.example: a broken data pipeline silently feeding a green dashboard hides a real failure

failure_modes: data wrong or stale but trusted
dashboard crowded so the signal is lost
acceptance_tests: data correctness and freshness verified before trust
each view maps to a decision and audience
revisit_triggers: a dashboard is not driving any decision

nodes.definition: Run a disciplined rhythm of reviews (daily/weekly/monthly/quarterly) that turns metrics and goals into decisions and follow-through.
contradictors: meeting-for-status manager who tracks no actions

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when reviews produce status but no decisions or closed actions

pros.claim: converts metrics and goals into tracked decisions and accountable follow-through
pros.example: a weekly review with an action log closes issues that a status email would let drift

cons.claim: cadence without decisions becomes status theater that consumes time
cons.example: a recurring meeting that reviews charts but assigns nothing wastes leadership hours

failure_modes: reviews track status but make no decisions
actions assigned but never followed up
acceptance_tests: each review produces decisions and owned actions
actions tracked to closure across cycles

nodes.definition: Identify operational and supply-chain disruption risks and build continuity, redundancy, and recovery plans so single failures do not halt the system.
contradictors: just-in-time-only manager who removes all slack

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a disruption occurs or the risk profile of supply/process changes

pros.claim: prevents a single failure from halting the whole operation
pros.example: a continuity plan and second source keep the line running when a port closes

cons.claim: redundancy and buffers cost money that pure efficiency would cut
cons.example: holding strategic buffer stock and a backup supplier raises carrying and qualification cost

failure_modes: single points of failure unmapped
continuity plans never tested
acceptance_tests: critical single points of failure identified and mitigated
continuity plans tested against scenarios
revisit_triggers: supply or process risk profile changes
a new single point of failure appears

nodes.definition: Govern the ongoing improvement loop (PDCA), prioritizing and validating changes so the operating system gets better without destabilizing it.
contradictors: change-everything-at-once manager with no control

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when improvement throughput stalls or changes destabilize operations

pros.claim: makes improvement a controlled, prioritized loop that locks in gains
pros.example: validating one change at a time with rollback keeps the system stable while it improves

cons.claim: too many simultaneous changes make cause and effect unattributable and risky
cons.example: running ten changes at once means a regression cannot be traced to its cause

failure_modes: changes not validated before standardizing
too many concurrent changes to attribute effect
acceptance_tests: each change validated against a baseline before lock-in
concurrent change limited to keep attribution

edges.why_related: process mapping targets the flow the operating model requires
edges.benefit_of_coupling: map is scoped to strategic priorities
edges.risk_of_conflict: mapping before strategy maps the wrong system
edges.example: a responsiveness strategy reframes which steps are mapped first
edges.resolution_rule: strategy dominates; remap if the operating model changes

edges.why_related: the constraint is found by analyzing the mapped flow
edges.benefit_of_coupling: constraint search runs on real step data
edges.risk_of_conflict: finding a constraint with no map mislabels the limit
edges.example: step cycle times on the VSM reveal where queue builds
edges.resolution_rule: mapping precedes constraint analysis; re-map if flow changes

edges.why_related: lean effort is aimed at the identified constraint
edges.risk_of_conflict: lean off the constraint yields no throughput
edges.example: kaizen is focused at the drum, not a random cell
edges.resolution_rule: constraint analysis dominates; re-target lean if constraint moves

edges.why_related: capacity is sized around the constraint
edges.benefit_of_coupling: capacity added where it lifts output
edges.risk_of_conflict: sizing capacity off-constraint wastes spend
edges.example: extra shifts are added at the bottleneck step
edges.resolution_rule: constraint location sets where capacity is added

edges.why_related: quality control targets steps and CTQs found in the map
edges.benefit_of_coupling: SPC is applied where variation hurts flow
edges.risk_of_conflict: controlling the wrong step misses real defects
edges.example: control charts placed at the step the map flags as variable
edges.resolution_rule: mapping informs where SPC is deployed

edges.why_related: forecasting horizon and granularity follow the operating model
edges.risk_of_conflict: forecasting with no strategy frame plans the wrong volumes
edges.example: a responsiveness strategy demands shorter, finer forecasts
edges.resolution_rule: strategy sets the forecasting frame

edges.why_related: inventory policy is computed from the forecast and its error
edges.benefit_of_coupling: safety stock sized to real variability
edges.risk_of_conflict: policy on a bad forecast stocks out or piles up
edges.example: reorder points use forecast error and lead time
edges.resolution_rule: forecast dominates; resize policy when error changes

edges.why_related: capacity is planned to the demand/S&OP plan
edges.risk_of_conflict: capacity to a wrong forecast under/over-builds
edges.example: staffing plan is built from the S&OP volume
edges.resolution_rule: forecast sets the capacity target

edges.why_related: sourcing strategy follows make-vs-buy and priorities
edges.risk_of_conflict: price-only sourcing can contradict strategy
edges.example: a flexibility strategy favors dual sourcing
edges.resolution_rule: strategy governs sourcing criteria

edges.why_related: distribution moves the stock the inventory policy positions
edges.risk_of_conflict: routing with no inventory plan misplaces goods
edges.example: DC stock levels set the replenishment routing
edges.resolution_rule: inventory plan sets what logistics must move

edges.why_related: structure is designed to execute the operating model
edges.risk_of_conflict: structure copied without strategy misaligns accountability
edges.example: a process-centric model favors cross-functional teams
edges.resolution_rule: operating model dominates structure design

edges.why_related: delegation is assigned within the decision-rights structure
edges.risk_of_conflict: delegating with no rights map causes conflict
edges.example: escalation thresholds follow the org's decision map
edges.resolution_rule: structure sets the frame for delegation

edges.why_related: roles to hire are defined by the structure
edges.risk_of_conflict: hiring before roles are defined seeks wrong profiles
edges.example: an org gap defines the role scorecard to hire for
edges.resolution_rule: structure defines roles before hiring

edges.why_related: headcount to hire is set by the capacity plan
edges.risk_of_conflict: hiring with no capacity plan over/under-staffs
edges.example: the capacity gap sizes the hiring requisition
edges.resolution_rule: capacity plan sizes staffing

edges.why_related: goals cascade from strategy and the operating model
edges.risk_of_conflict: goals with no strategy frame chase the wrong outcomes
edges.example: a cost-priority strategy sets cost-reduction key results
edges.resolution_rule: strategy dominates goal setting

edges.why_related: KPIs are chosen to measure the goals
edges.risk_of_conflict: metrics with no goals become vanity numbers
edges.example: each key result gets a leading and lagging KPI
edges.resolution_rule: goals dominate metric selection

edges.why_related: individual expectations are derived from team goals
edges.risk_of_conflict: reviews with no goal link rate the wrong things
edges.example: a team key result sets the manager's coaching focus
edges.resolution_rule: goals frame performance expectations

edges.why_related: the scorecard organizes the defined KPIs into perspectives
edges.benefit_of_coupling: balance is built on real metrics
edges.risk_of_conflict: a scorecard with no KPI base is empty
edges.example: KPIs are slotted into the four perspectives
edges.resolution_rule: KPIs precede scorecard assembly

edges.why_related: dashboards render the defined KPIs
edges.risk_of_conflict: dashboards before metric definitions show ad-hoc numbers
edges.example: each tile maps to a defined KPI
edges.resolution_rule: metric definitions precede dashboards

edges.why_related: reviews are structured around the KPIs
edges.risk_of_conflict: cadence with no metric base is status theater
edges.example: the weekly review walks the KPI set
edges.resolution_rule: metrics anchor the cadence

edges.why_related: the cadence reviews progress against goals
edges.risk_of_conflict: cadence with no goals tracks activity not outcomes
edges.example: the quarterly review scores key results
edges.resolution_rule: goals anchor the review rhythm

edges.why_related: cadence reviews consume the dashboards
edges.risk_of_conflict: reviewing without trusted dashboards wastes time
edges.example: the weekly meeting opens the live dashboard
edges.resolution_rule: build trusted dashboards before reviewing them

edges.why_related: improvement is prioritized from review outcomes
edges.risk_of_conflict: CI with no cadence loses prioritization
edges.example: review escalations seed the improvement backlog
edges.resolution_rule: cadence feeds the CI loop

edges.why_related: strategy constrains which metrics are legitimate
edges.risk_of_conflict: unconstrained metrics drift to vanity
edges.example: strategy forbids a metric that rewards the wrong behavior
edges.resolution_rule: strategy bounds the metric set

edges.why_related: capacity buffers constrain how lean the flow can run
edges.risk_of_conflict: over-lean removes the buffer capacity needs
edges.example: lean cannot cut the protective capacity buffer at the constraint
edges.resolution_rule: capacity buffer at the constraint is protected from lean cuts

edges.why_related: supplier lead time and MOQ constrain inventory policy
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring MOQ/lead time makes policy infeasible
edges.example: a long supplier lead time forces higher safety stock
edges.resolution_rule: supplier terms bound the inventory policy

edges.why_related: speed/flow pressure can trade off against variation control
edges.risk_of_conflict: cutting checks for flow raises defect escapes
edges.example: removing an inspection to speed flow risks more escapes
edges.resolution_rule: quality gate dominates for customer-critical CTQs; otherwise streamline

edges.why_related: capacity buffer and inventory buffer are substitute hedges against variability
edges.risk_of_conflict: double-buffering wastes cash; under-buffering stocks out
edges.example: you can hold safety stock or hold spare capacity, not pay fully for both
edges.resolution_rule: choose the cheaper buffer for the variability profile; record the tradeoff

edges.why_related: delegation speed trades off against control over high-risk decisions
edges.risk_of_conflict: over-delegating irreversible calls bypasses review
edges.example: a delegated quality waiver could ship a nonconforming lot
edges.resolution_rule: high-risk/irreversible decisions keep a review gate regardless of delegation level

edges.why_related: stretch goals tied to ratings trade ambition against honest measurement
edges.risk_of_conflict: tying aspirational OKRs to pay drives sandbagging and gaming
edges.example: scoring an aspirational key result like a commitment punishes ambition
edges.resolution_rule: separate aspirational goals from rated commitments; do not pay on stretch alone

edges.why_related: metric-based evaluation trades measurability against gaming (Goodhart)
edges.risk_of_conflict: optimizing a single rated metric distorts behavior
edges.example: rating on handle-time alone shortens calls and tanks resolution
edges.resolution_rule: pair rated metrics with guardrails and qualitative judgment

edges.why_related: a cost/efficiency push can conflict with a flexibility strategy
edges.risk_of_conflict: over-leaning a system meant to be flexible removes slack
edges.example: cost-cutting slack out of a responsive line slows it under surge
edges.resolution_rule: strategy's competitive priority dominates the efficiency push

edges.why_related: metric results can trigger a goal revisit
edges.risk_of_conflict: chronic metric miss may mean the goal is wrong
edges.example: a key result repeatedly missed triggers a goal review
edges.resolution_rule: revisit goals only at cycle boundaries; stop when KR is achievable or rescoped

edges.why_related: reviews can trigger re-planning of goals
edges.risk_of_conflict: reactively re-planning every review destabilizes focus
edges.example: a quarterly review reprioritizes the OKR set
edges.resolution_rule: re-plan goals at most once per cycle; stop when priorities are stable

edges.why_related: validated improvements trigger an update of the process map
edges.risk_of_conflict: an unupdated map after change misleads the next analysis
edges.example: a standardized improvement updates the VSM
edges.resolution_rule: update the map after each standardized change; stop when map matches the floor

edges.why_related: improvement can move the constraint and trigger re-analysis
edges.risk_of_conflict: acting on a stale constraint wastes effort
edges.example: elevating the old bottleneck shifts the limit elsewhere
edges.resolution_rule: re-run constraint analysis after each elevation; stop when the constraint is stable

edges.why_related: performance outcomes feed back into hiring profiles
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring performance data repeats mis-hires
edges.example: consistently weak hires trigger a scorecard revision
edges.resolution_rule: update hiring scorecards from performance data each cycle; stop when fit data is stable

edges.why_related: resilience requirements constrain how lean inventory may be
edges.risk_of_conflict: pure JIT inventory has no disruption cushion
edges.example: strategic buffer stock is held above the cost-optimal level for a critical part
edges.resolution_rule: resilience floor overrides cost-optimal inventory for critical items

edges.why_related: resilience requires sourcing redundancy for critical inputs
edges.risk_of_conflict: single-sourcing a critical input creates fragility
edges.example: a critical part is dual-sourced even at higher unit cost
edges.resolution_rule: resilience requires a second source for single points of failure

edges.why_related: both are buffering decisions against demand and supply variability
edges.risk_of_conflict: conflating them double-counts a hedge
edges.example: both translate variability into a protective buffer size
edges.resolution_rule: treat as related buffering methods; keep policies separate

conflict_axes.trigger: a lean/cost decision removes the slack that protects against disruption
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: for critical single points of failure, resilience floor dominates cost optimization; elsewhere optimize cost
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: the tradeoff changes a customer/financial outcome or an irreversible decision
conflict_axes.example: removing all buffer stock to cut carrying cost leaves no cushion for a supplier outage

conflict_axes.trigger: a cost-efficiency push conflicts with a flexibility/responsiveness strategy
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the strategy's competitive priority dominates; do not lean out slack a flexibility strategy needs
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: the tradeoff changes a customer/financial outcome or an irreversible decision
conflict_axes.example: cutting capacity slack to lower cost slows a line meant to flex under surge demand

conflict_axes.trigger: optimizing a non-constraint for local efficiency does not raise system throughput
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: constraint throughput dominates local utilization; subordinate non-constraints to the constraint
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: the tradeoff changes a customer/financial outcome or an irreversible decision
conflict_axes.example: maximizing a non-constraint machine's utilization just grows WIP before the real bottleneck

conflict_axes.trigger: removing checks to speed flow trades off against defect control
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: for customer-critical CTQs quality gate dominates; for non-critical steps streamline
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: the tradeoff changes a customer/financial outcome or an irreversible decision
conflict_axes.example: dropping an inspection to cut cycle time raises the escape rate on a critical feature

conflict_axes.trigger: fast delegated execution trades off against control over high-risk, irreversible decisions
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: irreversible/high-risk decision classes keep a review gate regardless of delegation level
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: the tradeoff changes a customer/financial outcome or an irreversible decision
conflict_axes.example: delegating a one-way-door supplier exit with no review risks an unrecoverable mistake

conflict_axes.trigger: stretch goals tied to ratings trade ambition against honest measurement and invite gaming
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: separate aspirational goals from rated commitments; do not pay on stretch alone
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: the tradeoff changes a customer/financial outcome or an irreversible decision
conflict_axes.example: scoring an aspirational OKR like a commitment drives sandbagging next cycle

conflict_axes.trigger: optimizing a single rated metric distorts behavior (Goodhart) versus balanced judgment
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: pair rated metrics with guardrails and qualitative judgment; balance perspectives
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: the tradeoff changes a customer/financial outcome or an irreversible decision
conflict_axes.example: rewarding handle-time alone shortens calls and tanks resolution quality

conflict_axes.trigger: running many improvements at once trades change velocity against stability and attribution
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: limit concurrent change and validate each against a baseline; stability gates standardization
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: the tradeoff changes a customer/financial outcome or an irreversible decision
conflict_axes.example: ten simultaneous changes make a regression impossible to trace to its cause

edge_cases.trigger: the constraint is misidentified or moves after a change
edge_cases.failure_mode: improvement and capital are spent off the real constraint
edge_cases.example: buying a faster upstream machine just grows the queue at the unmoved bottleneck
edge_cases.detection_method: compare step utilization and queue length against the claimed constraint after every change
resolution: re-run constraint analysis on current data
re-target improvement at the true constraint

edge_cases.trigger: a point forecast is used with no error band
edge_cases.failure_mode: inventory and capacity policy stock out or pile up periodically
edge_cases.example: planning to a single demand number guarantees recurring shortfalls
edge_cases.detection_method: check that forecast outputs carry an error/variance and that policy uses it
resolution: attach forecast error and recompute safety stock
track and feed back forecast accuracy

edge_cases.trigger: a critical input is single-sourced with no contingency
edge_cases.failure_mode: one supplier failure halts the operation
edge_cases.example: a sole supplier with no alternative can stop production at renewal
edge_cases.detection_method: scan the BOM for critical parts with one qualified supplier and no continuity plan
resolution: qualify a second source or hold strategic buffer
add a continuity plan and test it

edge_cases.trigger: a single rated metric is optimized at the expense of the goal
edge_cases.failure_mode: behavior is distorted and the real outcome degrades (Goodhart)
edge_cases.example: call-handle-time drops while first-contact resolution falls
edge_cases.detection_method: watch for a metric improving while its guardrail or outcome worsens
resolution: add a counter-metric/guardrail
rebalance rating onto the outcome and judgment

edge_cases.trigger: a dashboard shows wrong or stale data but is trusted
edge_cases.failure_mode: decisions are made on false signals
edge_cases.example: a broken pipeline silently feeds a green dashboard hiding a real failure
edge_cases.detection_method: reconcile dashboard values against source-of-truth and check data freshness timestamps
resolution: fix the pipeline and add freshness/quality checks
flag the view as unverified until reconciled

edge_cases.trigger: reviews track status but produce no decisions or owned actions
edge_cases.failure_mode: leadership time is spent without changing the operation
edge_cases.example: a recurring meeting reviews charts but assigns and closes nothing
edge_cases.detection_method: audit each review for decisions made and actions closed since last time
resolution: require a decision/action log per review
cut or restructure reviews that decide nothing

edge_cases.trigger: an irreversible high-risk decision is delegated with no review
edge_cases.failure_mode: an unrecoverable mistake is made without oversight
edge_cases.example: a delegated one-way-door supplier exit goes wrong with no recovery
edge_cases.detection_method: check that irreversible/high-risk decision classes carry a mandatory review gate
resolution: add a review gate for irreversible classes
record and approve the decision before action

edge_cases.trigger: the structure is changed frequently without a decision-rights map
edge_cases.failure_mode: coordination, accountability, and trust are repeatedly reset
edge_cases.example: a structure change every two quarters destroys institutional knowledge
edge_cases.detection_method: track reorg frequency and whether each change defined decision rights first
resolution: map decision rights before any reorg
stabilize structure and change only on real misfit

edge_cases.trigger: a non-constraint is optimized for local efficiency
edge_cases.failure_mode: WIP grows and system throughput does not improve
edge_cases.example: maxing a non-constraint machine's utilization just builds inventory before the bottleneck
edge_cases.detection_method: verify improvement targets the constraint and subordinates non-constraints
resolution: redirect effort to the constraint
subordinate non-constraint scheduling to the drum

edge_cases.trigger: too many changes are made at once with no baseline validation
edge_cases.failure_mode: a regression cannot be attributed and gains are not locked
edge_cases.example: ten changes ship together and a quality regression cannot be traced
edge_cases.detection_method: check concurrent change count and that each change was tested against a baseline
resolution: limit concurrent change
validate each change vs baseline before standardizing

edge_cases.trigger: capacity is planned to near-100% utilization on a variable process
edge_cases.failure_mode: lead time becomes unstable and queues explode under small surges
edge_cases.example: loading a variable line to 98% turns minor surges into long queues
edge_cases.detection_method: check planned utilization against demand/process variability and queueing limits
resolution: lower target utilization to leave a buffer
add capacity at the constraint

edge_cases.trigger: KPIs are defined with no link to a goal or decision
edge_cases.failure_mode: vanity metrics accumulate and dilute focus
edge_cases.example: a dashboard of pretty numbers that no review ever acts on
edge_cases.detection_method: verify each KPI maps to a goal/key result and drives a specific decision
resolution: drop metrics with no decision
tie remaining KPIs to goals and owners

workflow.objective: fix the operating model, competitive priorities, and cascaded goals
acceptance_tests: operating model and priorities written before process/metric design
goals are few and outcome-based
exit_criteria: operating model and goal cascade signed off
workflow.do_first_because: strategy anchors every process, supply-chain, org, and metric choice

workflow.objective: map the value stream and find the system constraint
acceptance_tests: map matches observed runs
constraint confirmed by utilization/queue data
exit_criteria: current-state map and constraint signed off
workflow.do_first_because: improvement and capacity must target the real constraint, not a symptom

workflow.objective: build the reconciled demand, inventory, and sourcing plan
gates: policy and sourcing tied to forecast and risk
acceptance_tests: forecast reported with error
critical items have contingency or second source
workflow.do_first_because: inventory, capacity, and logistics all derive from a reconciled demand plan

workflow.objective: size capacity, design distribution, and set resilience buffers
acceptance_tests: capacity plan accounts for variability
continuity plans tested against scenarios
exit_criteria: capacity, logistics, and continuity plans approved
workflow.do_first_because: capacity and resilience must be set before committing execution headcount and flow

workflow.objective: design structure, decision rights, and staff the capability gaps
gates: decision rights mapped before structure lock
irreversible classes carry a review gate
acceptance_tests: decision rights mapped before structure is locked
selection is structured and job-relevant
exit_criteria: structure, delegation, and hiring plan approved
workflow.do_first_because: structure and decision rights set how every later decision is made and by whom

workflow.objective: reduce waste at the constraint and bring quality into statistical control
gates: process in control before capability is claimed
acceptance_tests: lead-time/WIP reduction measured
process shown in control before capability reported
workflow.do_first_because: stable, in-control flow at the constraint is the baseline all later change is measured against

workflow.objective: define KPIs, balance perspectives, and build trusted dashboards
acceptance_tests: gameable KPIs paired with guardrails
data correctness and freshness verified before trust
workflow.do_first_because: metrics must be defined and trusted before they drive reviews and ratings

workflow.objective: run the review rhythm and manage performance against goals
gates: each review produces decisions and owned actions
acceptance_tests: actions tracked to closure
feedback given continuously not only at review
workflow.do_first_because: the cadence converts metrics and goals into accountable decisions and follow-through

workflow.objective: govern the prioritized, validated improvement loop
acceptance_tests: each change validated before standardizing
attribution preserved by limiting concurrent change
exit_criteria: improvement loop governed and gains standardized
workflow.do_first_because: improvement must be controlled so the system gets better without destabilizing

workflow.objective: review the full operating system against strategy and lock validated artifacts
acceptance_tests: high-risk/irreversible decisions reviewed
metrics still aligned to strategy
exit_criteria: operating system reviewed and approved for controlled lock
workflow.do_first_because: no artifact is hard-locked before dependency, validation, and human-review gates pass

priority_rationale.notes: root operating model anchors all work
goals frame all measurement and reviews
map grounds constraint and quality work
supplier commitments are costly to reverse
reorgs are disruptive and set decision flow
balances the metric set across perspectives
closes the loop and standardizes gains

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-risk or irreversible decision is rushed for speed
dominance_rules.rule: risk control dominates delivery speed for irreversible decisions
dominance_rules.example: do not skip a continuity review to exit a sole supplier faster

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value node is tempting to start before its prerequisite
dominance_rules.required_action: complete the prerequisite before finalizing the dependent node
dominance_rules.example: do not lock KPIs before goals and strategy are set

dominance_rules.trigger: local efficiency conflicts with the competitive priority
dominance_rules.rule: the strategic competitive priority dominates local optimization
dominance_rules.required_action: check local changes against the operating model before adopting
dominance_rules.example: do not lean out flexibility slack a responsiveness strategy needs

dominance_rules.trigger: a non-constraint is optimized for local utilization
dominance_rules.rule: system throughput at the constraint dominates local efficiency
dominance_rules.example: stop maximizing a non-constraint machine that only builds WIP

dominance_rules.trigger: results are pushed to lock before quality is in control
dominance_rules.rule: QA and statistical control dominate locking a change
dominance_rules.required_action: prove the process is in control before standardizing
dominance_rules.example: do not standardize a change whose Cpk has not been verified

dominance_rules.trigger: an irreversible decision could be made automatically or unilaterally
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates automation for irreversible/high-risk decisions
dominance_rules.required_action: route irreversible decisions to a human review gate
dominance_rules.example: a one-way-door supplier exit requires sign-off, not silent delegation

dominance_rules.trigger: a cost cut removes the slack protecting a single point of failure
dominance_rules.rule: resilience floor dominates cost optimization for critical SPOFs
dominance_rules.required_action: preserve buffer/redundancy on critical single points of failure
dominance_rules.example: keep strategic buffer stock on a critical sole-sourced part despite carrying cost

dominance_rules.trigger: a metric is optimized away from the goal it proxies
dominance_rules.rule: the goal/outcome dominates the proxy metric
dominance_rules.required_action: pair gameable metrics with guardrails tied to the outcome
dominance_rules.example: rebalance away from handle-time when resolution quality drops

dominance_rules.trigger: a precise number is asserted beyond what evidence supports
dominance_rules.required_action: label heuristic estimates as heuristic and avoid false precision
dominance_rules.example: report a forecast as a range with error, not a single confident number

dominance_rules.trigger: a dashboard is trusted without verifying data correctness
dominance_rules.required_action: verify correctness and freshness before a dashboard drives decisions
dominance_rules.example: reconcile a green dashboard against source-of-truth before acting on it

dominance_rules.trigger: many changes are launched at once without attribution control
dominance_rules.rule: operational stability and attribution dominate change velocity
dominance_rules.required_action: limit concurrent change and validate each against a baseline
dominance_rules.example: stage ten proposed changes instead of shipping them all in one week

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix the operating model and priorities before designing processes or metrics
anti_rework_rules.rationale: process and metric work built on no strategy optimizes the wrong thing
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: process or KPI design starts with no written operating model
anti_rework_rules.example: do not map and lean a process before the competitive priority is set

anti_rework_rules.rationale: metrics with no goal become vanity numbers and get reworked
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: KPIs defined with no linked goal
anti_rework_rules.example: do not build a dashboard before the OKRs exist

anti_rework_rules.rule: map the value stream before identifying the constraint
anti_rework_rules.rationale: finding a constraint with no map mislabels the limit and wastes improvement
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: constraint asserted with no validated map
anti_rework_rules.example: do not run a kaizen before the bottleneck is confirmed on the map

anti_rework_rules.rule: identify the constraint before targeting lean/quality effort
anti_rework_rules.rationale: improvement off the constraint yields no throughput and is redone
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: improvement effort spent on a non-constraint
anti_rework_rules.example: do not add capacity before knowing where the constraint is

anti_rework_rules.rule: produce a forecast with error before setting inventory/capacity policy
anti_rework_rules.rationale: policy on a bad forecast stocks out or piles up and is reworked
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: inventory or capacity policy set with no forecast error
anti_rework_rules.example: do not size safety stock before forecast error is known

anti_rework_rules.rule: map decision rights before locking the org structure
anti_rework_rules.rationale: structure with no decision-rights map causes conflict and reorgs
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: structure locked with no decision-rights map
anti_rework_rules.example: do not publish an org chart before decision rights are mapped

anti_rework_rules.rule: define roles from the structure before hiring
anti_rework_rules.rationale: hiring before roles are defined seeks the wrong profiles and mis-hires
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: sourcing starts with no role scorecard
anti_rework_rules.example: do not open a requisition before the role is defined

anti_rework_rules.rule: show the process in statistical control before claiming capability
anti_rework_rules.rationale: capability claimed on an out-of-control process is invalid and redone
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: Cpk reported from an unstable process
anti_rework_rules.example: do not report Cpk before control charts show stability

anti_rework_rules.rule: verify dashboard data before it drives reviews
anti_rework_rules.rationale: decisions on wrong/stale data are reworked after the error is found
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a review acts on an unverified dashboard
anti_rework_rules.example: do not run the weekly review on an unreconciled dashboard

anti_rework_rules.rule: validate each change against a baseline before standardizing
anti_rework_rules.rationale: standardizing an unvalidated change locks in a possible regression
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a change standardized with no baseline comparison
anti_rework_rules.example: do not write standard work for a change whose effect was never measured

iteration_protocol.trigger: a validation check or operational metric breaches its threshold
iteration_protocol.detection: validator or dashboard flags a breach
acceptance_tests: each breach recorded with severity

iteration_protocol.trigger: multiple defects compete for limited change capacity
iteration_protocol.detection: rank by risk x reversibility x throughput impact
acceptance_tests: queue ordered by risk-adjusted leverage

iteration_protocol.trigger: a fix touches a high-coupling node
iteration_protocol.detection: trace dependents via edges and priority order
acceptance_tests: all dependents of the changed node identified

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect is assigned for repair
iteration_protocol.detection: route to the owning subsystem per repair_routing
acceptance_tests: fix applied by the correct owner

iteration_protocol.trigger: a change is applied to a locked or high-coupling component
iteration_protocol.detection: re-run validators and affected acceptance tests
acceptance_tests: affected checks pass after the fix

iteration_protocol.trigger: new evidence shifts a node's importance or risk
iteration_protocol.detection: compare posterior delta against the revisit threshold
acceptance_tests: scores recomputed within tolerance
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: posterior delta below the revisit threshold

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect is high-risk, irreversible, or crosses a human-review threshold
acceptance_tests: high-risk items reviewed by a human

iteration_protocol.trigger: a locked artifact must change after a dependency or validation shift
iteration_protocol.detection: verify a change-control record exists before downgrade
acceptance_tests: downgrade carries a change-control record and revalidation
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no locked artifact changes without a record

test_cases.input_summary: a small service operation with stable demand
a plant with one clear bottleneck

expected_properties: OPS_RISK_RESILIENCE triggers a second source or buffer

test_cases.input_summary: a single KPI is tied to ratings

change_triggers: business strategy or competitive priority changes
org operating model or scale changes
a metric is gamed or decouples from its outcome
version_increment_rules: increment on any change to a hard-locked operating-model or sourcing artifact
increment when the operating model or competitive priorities change
lock_downgrade_rules: downgrade requires a change-control record and revalidation
high-coupling node downgrade forces revalidation of all dependents
human_approval_required_for: outlier delegation of an irreversible decision
